title: On the Soul, to Tatian
author: Gregory Thaumaturgus
edition: Opera omnia, Greek and Latin (Paris, 1622), Latin column (Disputatio de Anima ad Tatianum): preface and chapters I-VII; Greek column OCR damaged
blurb: Gregory Thaumaturgus, On the Soul, to Tatian: a fresh English translation of the whole short treatise. Arguing from reason alone, without Scripture proofs, it shows that the soul is known by its effects, exists, is a substance, is not a body, is simple, is immortal and shares in reason. Scholars dispute whether Gregory wrote it.
era_note: The Disputatio de Anima ad Tatianum stands under Gregory Thaumaturgus's name in the third-century Neocaesarean tradition; later Latin presentation and disputed authenticity are disclosed.
first_english_note: Prior English exists (ANF 6 Salmond, PD); this is a fresh English translation of the whole treatise from the Latin.

text_history.method: Fresh English translation of the whole treatise (preface and chapters I-VII) from the Latin column of the Opera omnia print (Paris, 1622), read from the page images; the Greek column's OCR is too damaged to use; scholia stripped; ANF 6 consulted only as a sense check for the preface; the edition's blurred margin variants are noted but not adopted; earlier scaffold paraphrase discarded.

witnesses.name: Opera omnia, Greek and Latin (Paris: Sonnius, Morel and Cramoisy, 1622), page images

joins.note: Long-s and column joins expanded from the Latin face; sense checked against the inquiry program that follows.
